summary: The SOP has a strong four-block structure, clear guardrails, and thorough catalog checks, but contains critical execution bugs in its write-fencing, clone subscription handling, rollback window math, and precheck coverage of template1 and PG 18 collation blockers. In addition, several source entries (S-10 and S-34 through S-37), stats coverage queries, and Google DMS-specific claims in the logical branch need correction before teams rely on this procedure in production.

findings.claim: Setting `ALTER DATABASE <db> SET default_transaction_read_only = on` at T-0 causes subsequent in-window writes and DDL (final and post-upgrade sentinel inserts, `ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... DISABLE`, `ALTER EXTENSION ... UPDATE`) to fail unless overridden per session, and persists into the pre-upgrade backup so a restored recovery instance comes up read-only. In addition, opening pooler connections during read-only smoke tests (line 287) before lifting the database setting (line 288) leaves pooled backend sessions stuck in read-only mode.
findings.evidence: sop.md line 205–207: "Set `ALTER DATABASE <db> SET default_transaction_read_only = on` for each app database, then end the remaining app sessions... Insert one final sentinel row"; line 217: "Cloud SQL takes a pre-upgrade backup automatically, 'immediately before starting the upgrade' [S-01]"; lines 287–288: "Bring up the pooler and routing with the databases still read-only, then run validation and read-only smoke tests... Reopen writes: lift the read-only setting, resume the pooler"; lines 240–245 and 292–299 (Rollback) never reset `default_transaction_read_only` on the recovery instance, and Block 2 never resets it at all. Per PostgreSQL documentation (https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/sql-alterdatabase.html), `ALTER DATABASE ... SET` saves session defaults in `pg_db_role_setting` that apply at session start and block writes/DDL unless `SET default_transaction_read_only = off` is run in the session.
findings.suggested_fix: Instruct the DBA and CDC sessions to set `SET default_transaction_read_only = off` when inserting sentinels, disabling subscriptions, or updating extensions, and add an explicit `ALTER DATABASE <db> RESET default_transaction_read_only` step both in Block 2 and in the rollback procedure after restoring the pre-upgrade backup. At cutover reopen (line 288), reconnect or recycle pooler backend connections after lifting `default_transaction_read_only` so sessions opened during read-only smoke tests do not remain read-only.

findings.claim: Cloning a production instance that has active inbound logical subscriptions (`pg_subscription`) starts logical replication workers on the clone that connect to the upstream production publisher's slots and consume WAL meant for production, and disabling subscriptions at T+5 before the T+10 pre-upgrade backup leaves them disabled after a rollback restore.
findings.evidence: sop.md line 176: "1. Clone production." followed by line 216: "6. Drain CDC... and disable inbound subscriptions"; line 283–284: "T+5 | Drain CDC... and disable inbound subscriptions" before "T+10 | Start the upgrade" (when the pre-upgrade backup is taken per [S-01]); lines 240–245 and 292–299 (Rollback) list recreating outbound slots on the recovery instance but omit re-enabling inbound subscriptions (`ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... ENABLE`). In PostgreSQL (https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/logical-replication-subscription.html), a cloned database retains `pg_subscription.subenabled = true` and `subconninfo`/`subslotname` immediately upon boot.
findings.suggested_fix: In Block 2 Step 1, immediately disable or drop all `pg_subscription` entries on the clone as soon as it boots (and never re-enable them against a production upstream publisher). In Block 2 Step 14 and Block 3 Rollback, add a step to run `ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... ENABLE` on the recovery instance before reopening.

findings.claim: Gates G2.1 and G2.6 never verify that the forward upgrade through Go/No-Go 2 plus the rehearsed rollback fit within the maintenance window, allowing the latest rollback decision time (`window end - 1.25 * rollback duration`) to fall before the upgrade or Go/No-Go 2 completes.
findings.evidence: sop.md line 154: "Prove with timings, on a production clone, that the runbook and the rollback fit the window, twice in a row"; line 164 (G2.1): "Two rehearsals in a row finish the in-window steps within 75% of the window" (where Step 13 on line 238 stops the window clock before Step 14's rollback); line 170 (G2.6): "The full rollback was rehearsed and timed through app validation, and the runbook states the latest rollback decision time"; line 284: "At the latest rollback decision time (window end minus 1.25 times the rehearsed rollback duration), roll back unless the upgrade has finished"; line 292: "Until the first write on the new version (including a failure after go or no-go 2, if writes haven't reopened yet), run the rehearsed rollback".
findings.suggested_fix: Update Gate G2.1/G2.6 so the rehearsed time to reach Go/No-Go 2 (with its 25% margin) plus 1.25 times the rehearsed rollback duration must be less than or equal to the maintenance window. If that sum exceeds the window, require expanding the window or switching to the logical branch in the decision record.

findings.claim: The precheck psql loop and reading guide explicitly exclude `template1` (`AND NOT datistemplate`), even though `pg_upgrade` and Cloud SQL connect to, check, and upgrade `template1` alongside customer databases.
findings.evidence: precheck.sql line 23: "for db in $(psql "<connection>" -XAtc "SELECT datname FROM pg_database WHERE datallowconn AND NOT datistemplate AND datname NOT IN ('cloudsqladmin','rdsadmin','azure_maintenance','azure_sys')"); do"; precheck-reading-guide.md line 12: "Each customer database in section 2a with `datallowconn = t` has its own file. Templates and provider-internal databases (`cloudsqladmin`, `rdsadmin`, `azure_maintenance`, `azure_sys`) don't count." Per [S-22] (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/postgres/postgres/REL_18_STABLE/src/bin/pg_upgrade/check.c) and [S-01], `pg_upgrade` checks all databases where `datallowconn` is true (including `template1`) and fails if `template1` contains unsupported column types, NOT NULL mismatches, or un-upgraded extensions such as `pg_squeeze` or `postgis`.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove `AND NOT datistemplate` from `precheck.sql` line 23 (since `datallowconn` already excludes `template0`) and update `precheck-reading-guide.md` line 12 and `sop.md` line 66 so `template1` is included in the per-database precheck and extension/analyze steps.

findings.claim: Task B1-14 groups primary and foreign key pairs on nondeterministic collations under the post-upgrade 'Reindex inventory' and allows them to become a 'timed runbook step', even though `pg_upgrade`'s schema restore refuses them during the upgrade itself; moreover, `precheck.sql` has no query to detect them or to identify `pg_trgm`, full-text search, or `btree_gist` float4/float8 indexes.
findings.evidence: sop.md line 140 (B1-14): "Reindex inventory: `btree_gist` float opclasses and `ltree` after 14.24 [S-21]; full-text search and `pg_trgm` indexes on clusters whose default collation provider isn't libc [S-17]; primary and foreign key pairs on nondeterministic collations, which pg_upgrade's restore refuses [S-17]. Each becomes a fix task or a timed runbook step."; sop.md line 219: "run the reindex steps from B1-14"; precheck.sql lines 263–271 (section 8g) only checks `WHERE e.extname IN ('btree_gist', 'ltree', 'vector')` without selecting `oc.opcname` and has no query for nondeterministic collations on PK/FK pairs, non-libc collations, `pg_trgm`, or full-text search indexes. Per [S-17] (https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/release-18.html, "Require primary/foreign key relationships to use either deterministic collations"), incompatible PK/FK collations fail during `pg_upgrade` restore.
findings.suggested_fix: Move PK/FK nondeterministic collation checks into `precheck.sql` section 6 (as a pre-upgrade catalog blocker for B1-02 and G0.4/G1.1, never a post-upgrade runbook step). Expand `precheck.sql` section 8g to include `oc.opcname`, `pg_trgm` and full-text search indexes, and `pg_collation` provider metadata so agents have the inputs needed for B1-14.

findings.claim: `precheck.sql` section 6g omits `CHECK` constraints even though `sop.md` line 80 states that section 6g covers functions used in `CHECK` constraints, and B1-02 assumes all 6g functions can be altered with `search_path` even when owned by extensions.
findings.evidence: sop.md line 80: "search_path functions (section 6g). From PG 17, maintenance runs with a safe `search_path` [S-18], so a function used in an index, materialized view, generated column or CHECK constraint that relies on `search_path` can fail... Cloud SQL documents only earthdistance's `ll_to_earth` case [S-01]. Fix every row before the rehearsal"; sop.md line 128 (B1-02): "pin `search_path` on the 6g functions"; precheck.sql lines 188–211 only filters `d.classid` in `('pg_class', 'pg_rewrite', 'pg_attrdef')` and excludes `d.classid = 'pg_constraint'::regclass`. On Cloud SQL [S-01, S-05], extension functions like `ll_to_earth` are owned by `cloudsqladmin` and cannot be modified via `ALTER FUNCTION` by `cloudsqlsuperuser`.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `OR (d.classid = 'pg_constraint'::regclass AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint c WHERE c.oid = d.objid AND c.contype = 'c'))` to `precheck.sql` section 6g. In `sop.md` B1-02 and `precheck-reading-guide.md` line 52, note that extension-owned functions such as `ll_to_earth` cannot be altered directly on Cloud SQL and require updating the extension or replacing the expression.

findings.claim: The stats coverage queries in Block 2 (Step 3 and Step 9) equate non-empty tables with `pg_relation_size(c.oid) > 0` and assume the database owner can read `pg_stats` for all tables, causing false negatives on tables with 0 live rows (but allocated pages), tables owned by other roles, or tables with active RLS.
findings.evidence: sop.md line 166 (G2.3): "In every database, every non-empty table the analyze role can read has planner stats after the upgrade"; lines 185–199 (Step 3): "as the database owner... WHERE ... has_table_privilege(c.oid, 'SELECT') AND pg_relation_size(c.oid) > 0"; lines 220–232 (Step 9): "Run every step as the database owner: database owners may analyze all tables in their database [S-16]... WHERE c.relkind IN ('r', 'm', 'p') ... AND (c.relkind = 'p' OR pg_relation_size(c.oid) > 0) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_stats s...)". In PostgreSQL (https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/view-pg-stats.html), `ANALYZE` writes no `pg_statistic` rows for a table with 0 live tuples even when `pg_relation_size(c.oid) > 0` from prior deletes, and `pg_stats` hides rows unless the caller has column `SELECT` privilege (which database ownership alone does not grant) and RLS is inactive; Step 3 also omits `relkind = 'p'`, `pg_temp%` filtering, and `pg_statistic_ext` that Step 9 checks.
findings.suggested_fix: Ensure the analyze role is also granted `pg_read_all_data` (or check `pg_class.reltuples` / `pg_stat_all_tables.last_analyze`), exclude `pg_temp%` schemas, and align Step 3 and Step 9 on `relkind` and `pg_stats_ext` coverage as well as tables that have `pg_relation_size(c.oid) > 0` but `reltuples = 0`.

findings.claim: When `pg_authid` is unreadable (always true on Cloud SQL), `precheck.sql` outputs no list of login roles at all, leaving Gate G1.4 unable to verify that every password-login role was rotated; additionally, `tracker-schema.md` has no valid `Auth` enum value for password-authenticated roles in Block 0 when MD5 vs SCRAM is unknown.
findings.evidence: precheck.sql lines 214–219: "\if :can_read_authid / SELECT rolname FROM pg_authid WHERE rolcanlogin AND rolpassword LIKE 'md5%' ORDER BY 1; / \else / \echo 'This role cannot read pg_authid (expected for cloudsqlsuperuser), so md5 roles are not listed.' / \endif" (and line 85 only selects `count(*) FROM pg_roles`). sop.md line 118 (G1.4): "Every password-login role has had its password reset under `scram-sha-256`, or has its owner's waiver | A rotation log listing each role and date"; sop.md line 37 (G0.1): "Every repo and consumer row has an owner, an auth method and a connection path"; readiness-scan.md line 11: "Auth method: password (MD5 or SCRAM unknown from code)"; tracker-schema.md line 31: "Auth | `scram`, `md5`, `iam`, `cert`, `unknown`".
findings.suggested_fix: Add `SELECT rolname, rolconnlimit, rolvaliduntil FROM pg_roles WHERE rolcanlogin AND rolname !~ '^(pg_|cloudsql|rds|azure_)' ORDER BY 1;` to `precheck.sql` section 7 so the full login-role inventory is always captured. In `tracker-schema.md` line 31, either allow `password` in `Auth` during Block 0 (upgraded to `scram` at G1.4) or clarify in G0.1 that `unknown` is accepted for MD5-vs-SCRAM until G1.4.

findings.claim: Section 6 ('Logical branch') states Google Cloud DMS behaviors from `[S-13]`—that sequences sync automatically at promotion and that destination backups/PITR are suspended during replication—as general rules for all logical paths (`DMS, pglogical or pgcopydb`), omits Section 6 from Section 8 ('Adapting to another provider'), and omits running `ANALYZE` on the logical destination.
findings.evidence: sop.md line 314: "This template covers the logical path (DMS, pglogical or pgcopydb) only in outline."; line 322: "Sequences sync only at promotion [S-13]."; line 324: "Automated backups and point-in-time recovery are suspended on the destination during continuous replication [S-13]."; lines 340–347 (Section 8) omit Section 6. Per [S-13] (sources.json lines 183–195), automatic sequence sync during promotion and suspended destination backups/PITR are specific to Google Cloud DMS; in native PostgreSQL logical replication, `pglogical`, or `pgcopydb` [S-29], sequences are not automatically synchronized by a promotion button and must be explicitly copied after fencing writes to avoid primary-key collisions.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark the sequence promotion sync and backup/PITR suspension bullets in Section 6 as specific to Google Cloud DMS, require an explicit post-fence sequence synchronization step for `pglogical`/`pgcopydb`/native logical replication, add a pre-cutover `ANALYZE` step on the logical target, and reference Section 6 in Section 8.

findings.claim: Neither Block 2 Step 6 nor Block 3 `T+5` instructs CDC owners to stop outbound CDC consumers after they drain, and the sentinel table is only added to publications on the clone in Block 2 Step 4 with no Block 1 task to create and publish it in production before the migration freeze.
findings.evidence: sop.md line 202 (Block 2 Step 4): "Add a small sentinel table to its publication on the clone, insert numbered rows"; lines 210–216 (Block 2 Step 6): "Drain CDC. A consumer is drained when the final sentinel has arrived downstream and its slot's `confirmed_flush_lsn` stopped advancing... Record each logical slot's name, plugin and consumer, and disable inbound subscriptions"; line 282 (`T-0`): "Insert the final sentinel"; line 283 (`T+5`): "Drain CDC (final sentinel delivered, `confirmed_flush_lsn` stable), record slots, and disable inbound subscriptions"; line 286: "Create the new slots, but don't start CDC consumers yet".
findings.suggested_fix: Add a task in Block 1 (`B1-02`/`B1-05`) to create the sentinel table and add it to each production publication before the T-7 migration freeze. In Block 2 Step 6 and Block 3 `T+5`, explicitly instruct CDC owners to stop outbound CDC connectors once drained so they do not auto-reconnect or auto-create slots during the upgrade window.

findings.claim: Block 0 and Gate G1.1 require pre-upgrade extension blockers (`PostGIS` < 3.6.0, `pg_squeeze` < 1.8, `pg_ivm`, `adminpack`, and section 8f outdated extensions) and section `5b`/`6b`/`6c` blockers to be fixed in production on the source version during Block 1, but Block 1's task table (`B1-02` and `B1-06`) only produces a runbook section for extensions and omits `5b`/`6b`/`6c` fixes.
findings.evidence: sop.md lines 83–87: "Cloud SQL 18 needs PostGIS 3.6.0, and `pg_squeeze` 1.8 [S-01]. `pg_ivm` blocks the MVU [S-01]. `adminpack` is gone in 17 [S-18]... extensions behind their default version (kit section 8f) need `ALTER EXTENSION ... UPDATE`"; line 115 (G1.1): "Every blocker from G0.3 and G0.4 is fixed in production on the source version"; line 128 (B1-02): "Catalog fixes: pin `search_path` on the 6g functions, add the missing NOT NULLs from 6d, change the reg* columns from 6a"; line 132 (B1-06): "Extensions: list the target versions and the `ALTER EXTENSION` steps | Agent | Runbook section". Also, `precheck-reading-guide.md` line 40 omits the `pg_squeeze` 1.8 floor from `[S-01]`.
findings.suggested_fix: Update `B1-06` (Run by: `Both`) to include applying required pre-upgrade `ALTER EXTENSION ... UPDATE` / `DROP EXTENSION` changes on the source instance before G1.1 (as well as listing post-upgrade runbook steps), add `5b`, `6b`, and `6c` blocker remediation to `B1-02`, and add `pg_squeeze` to `precheck-reading-guide.md` line 40.

findings.claim: Sources `S-34` through `S-37` are cited in `sop.md` and `precheck-reading-guide.md` as verified facts but are completely missing from `sources.md` and lack `status`, `lastChecked`, and `verified` fields in `sources.json`; additionally, `S-10` has status `changed` in `sources.json` and `sources.md` yet `sop.md` cites it as Verified instead of marking it Unverified.
findings.evidence: sources.md line 3: "A source whose quotes have moved is marked `changed`, and one that can't be fetched is marked `unreachable`. Treat claims that cite it as Unverified until someone rechecks."; sources.md line 24: "| S-10 | ... | changed 2026-11-04 |"; sop.md line 87: "Cloud SQL maintenance installs new extension binaries but doesn't update an extension's catalog version [S-10]."; sources.json lines 621–656 (`S-34`, `S-35`, `S-36`, `S-37`) omit `lastChecked`, `status`, and `verified` and are absent from `sources.md` (which jumps from `S-33` on line 47 to `S-40` on line 48), contradicting `sop.md` line 19 ("`[S-nn]` points to a row in `sources.md`. Each row lists the exact quotes it was verified against").
findings.suggested_fix: Re-verify `S-10` and `S-34` through `S-37` (or mark `[S-10]` claims as `Unverified` in `sop.md` and `precheck-reading-guide.md` until rechecked), add `lastChecked`, `status`, and `verified` to `S-34`–`S-37` in `sources.json`, and regenerate `sources.md`.

findings.claim: Task B1-04 checks that application drivers support SCRAM before rotating passwords to `scram-sha-256`, but omits checking connection pooler authentication (`auth_type` / `userlist.txt` / `auth_query`), and Block 3 `T+10` (line 284) makes an uncited, unlabeled claim about when a restore can start.
findings.evidence: sop.md line 130 (B1-04): "Auth: reset every password-login role's password under SCRAM, and check that each driver supports SCRAM"; line 284 (`T+10`): "Cloud SQL can cancel only during the main upgrade phase, and not when replicas are included [S-01]. A restore starts only after the operation is cancelled or has ended." (no `[S-nn]` citation or `Verified`/`Inferred`/`Unverified` label, and `[S-01]` restores the pre-upgrade backup to a separate recovery instance); line 43 (G0.7): "Questions for the provider have been sent, and someone owns tracking the replies | Question rows with an owner" (does not require evidence that the questions were actually sent).
findings.suggested_fix: Include connection pooler SCRAM configuration (`auth_type`, `userlist.txt`, or `auth_query`) in `B1-04`, label or remove the uncited restore sentence on line 284, and require a support-case/message link or `Waiting on provider` status in Gate G0.7's evidence.
